subsystem: assurance (red team, real-world gate, invariant monitor, long-run harness, invention/counterfactual forks, fidelity register, analytics)
summary:
Crucible 4.0's assurance layer runs on the evaluator side and reads authoritative state and the event log. None of it is a tool. It has six parts:

(1) Red team (src/crucible/redteam). A three-phase Probe contract: an operator sets up, the attacker acts only through World.execute (while it acts, system_call raises ProbeViolation), and an independent Evaluator gives the verdict. After every probe, integrity_postcheck checks invariants, the ledger, conservation and exact replay, and can override a "held" verdict. The catalogue has 81 probes in 7 attack classes; 25 of them are per-family mechanism scans. A KNOWN_OPEN ratchet lists 1 open finding (an event-log suffix rewrite that needs an external anchor), and deliberately vulnerable toys show the framework can catch real holes. Latest report: 79 held, 1 integrity_break, 1 not_applicable.

(2) Real-world gate (src/crucible/realworld). RealWorldBridge refuses everything without an operator-owned authorisation file. It enforces an allow-list after DNS resolution and pins each connection to the checked address. It blocks private and metadata addresses, enforces budgets and rate limits, and needs live approval for any action other than GET/HEAD. Everything goes into a blake2b hash-chained log. Outcomes come only from measure(fn). RealWorldResult refuses json, pickle and copy, and SealedHoldoutGuard counts holdout evaluations.

(3) InvariantMonitor (evaluation/invariants.py). It recomputes ledger, contract, compute, company, scheduler, inventory and process laws from raw tables, on demand or every N simulated seconds.

(4) run_long (evaluation/longrun.py). Daily and weekly liveness relative to recent levels per need-sector, collapse and recovery with a proximate cause, recorded operator shocks, snapshot and resume, and a final replay digest check. Recorded runs: 365 days x 3 seeds (ow_market), 180 x 2 (ow_frontier) and 90 x 2 (ow_heldout), all healthy, no focal agents.

(5) Forks. invention.py diffs a structural census of matched forks and places each difference by causal order 0-4, with no_response and removal arms and multi-seed suites. counterfactual.py provides fork_compare and Intervention factories.

(6) fidelity.py. A 55-mechanism register (37 plausible-hypothesis, 18 known-unrealistic, 0 calibrated), validate_register, which refuses a calibration claim without in-repo evidence, nine simulated measures, all marked "no reference data", and fidelity_report.

analytics (trace and metrics_export) adds read-only causal debugging over the event log.

Everything here is architecture-agnostic: it is learner-independent and reads state, not agent claims. The main gaps against v5 are:
- no social, content or audience coverage in the probes, invariants, liveness, census or register;
- no empirical calibration;
- only one established causal chain class (compute capacity);
- no cross-world contamination probe;
- scale limits (2M-event log retention, invariant checks that scan the whole history).

data_model_and_state:
Assurance code holds almost no state of its own. It reads the kernel's authoritative state (world.state.tables / arrays / meta), the in-memory event log (world.log, log_base, events_range) and the store.

- Red team: per-run state lives on a shallow copy of each Probe. The Evaluator holds a baseline {seq, t, attacker_wealth}. controlled_closure() expands attacker principals to orgs they own or administer and to the service principals they operate. Reports are plain JSON (schema crucible-redteam/1).
- InvariantMonitor: keeps violations (first detection per (kind, where)) and _txn_seq (txn id -> seq of the posting event). It also keeps the stock base and delta tallies, proc_failures, the periodic-job registry and money facts. It subscribes via world.listeners and runs check() on 'time'/'proc' events once every_s has elapsed, outside transactions. It reads private kernel structures (world._heap, world.processes).
- run_long: _Recorder (listener with per-day tallies, an incident list and bytes per event via json.dumps), _Liveness (trailing served history per sector, open episodes) and the monitor. Resume state is pickled to <label>.state.pkl next to the <label>.snap world snapshot (World.snapshot_blob, pickle + zlib).
- Invention/counterfactual: worlds forked from one snapshot_blob into in-memory World.from_blob copies. Interventions are recorded system_calls, except set_params, which mutates spec.params and emits an internal 'note' event whose applier is a no-op (core/kernel.py:385).
- Fidelity: a static Python list REGISTER of frozen Mechanism dataclasses keyed by string id (e.g. 'demand.price_response'), mapped to kernel module names.
- Real-world: an on-disk JSONL chain {i, prev, body, hash} (blake2b-16, GENESIS '0'*32, O_APPEND, fsync per record). Budgets and holdout counts are recomputed from the log on open, so they survive restarts. Results are kept only in RealWorldResult objects and *.realworld.json files.
- Ids: principals 'p:<handle>', organisations 'o:<handle>', services 'svc:<host>'. Entity ids follow kernel prefixes (acct_, ctr_, lst_, inst_, ...). Probe names are dotted 'class.what[param]'.
extension_points: New probe module: add a module with `probes() -> list[Probe]` to the tuple at src/crucible/redteam/suite.py:15. New findings must be added to KNOWN_OPEN (suite.py:32) or tests/test_redteam.py fails. MUST_HOLD in tests/test_redteam.py:18 lists probes that must hold.

v5 world factory for the red team: run_probes(factory, probes) accepts any callable. Probe.world requirements are passed as kwargs through _call_factory (framework.py:420); a factory that lacks a requested kwarg gives not_applicable. Families can also be added through default_world_factory(family=..., extra_modules=...) (framework.py:350).

Canary coverage for new private state: extend the table/field list and the module-config list in hidden_canaries (src/crucible/redteam/leakage.py:49-102), e.g. participant memories, recommender internals, neural participant hidden states, private messages.

Mechanism-family leak scans: independence.mechanism_families() (independence.py:512) picks up every registered FAMILIES entry starting with 'mech_' (excluding '_tools') hosted by the 'rig' module. New Tier 1 families registered that way are scanned automatically; other prefixes are not.
Static reachability guard: extend StaticReachability.FORBIDDEN (independence.py:151) with v5 evaluator, verifier, sealed-set and dataset packages so world mechanics cannot import them.

InvariantMonitor laws: add per-subsystem checks in check() (invariants.py:128-160), e.g. a _social(st) or _audience(st) check, and event tallies in _on_event (invariants.py:108). Violation(kind, where, seq, t, amounts, detail) is generic.

Long-run liveness: _Recorder.on_event (longrun.py:116) for new activity counters (posts, views, community joins, recurring payments); _Liveness.day takes any 'sectors' dict (longrun.py:279); new shock kinds in inject_shock (longrun.py:324) backed by new operator-only endpoints on the Disturb module (longrun.py:55, host 'admin'); hooks before_day(world, day), progress(row), agents=[(handle, policy, endowment)].

Causal chains (10.3/Gate L): extend invention.census (invention.py:49) with social, content, community and research tables, and consequences() (invention.py:201) with order placement for them. New Intervention factories go in counterfactual.py:64-111 (e.g. remove_content, ban_community, disable_recommender, withdraw_lineage). Arm(intervention, at_day, provenance) gives the removal arms.

Fidelity register: append Mechanism entries via _m(...) in REGISTER (fidelity.py:71-271). Change STATUSES/KINDS (fidelity.py:43-44) and Mechanism fields (fidelity.py:50) for the v5 six-level scheme plus population/platform/time-period/limitations. validate_register (fidelity.py:280) is where to enforce 'not calibrated merely because it is a neural network'. New measures go in MEASURES (fidelity.py:727). Coverage is checked by uncovered_modules (fidelity.py:331) over modules_with_behavioural_rules, which covers packages crucible.economy/actors/worlds/mechanisms/usefulness or any module with a scheduled process (fidelity.py:316).

Real-world experiments: RealWorldBridge.measure(name, fn) / evaluate_holdout (bridge.py:318/:343) are the only result sources. Call forbid_in_this_process() (bridge.py:55) at the start of world-hosting entrypoints, and assert_no_real_world() (results.py:82) in synthetic results writers.
Acceptance evidence: the `acceptance` fixture (tests/conftest.py:48) writes machine-readable gate records; ACCEPTANCE_DIR (conftest.py:13) would need a v5 subdirectory or prefix.

Store anchors: storage.base.make_anchor(world) / verify_anchor(store, anchor) (src/crucible/storage/base.py:110/:117) exist but are not called by run_long or any harness; this is where the open suffix-rewrite finding can be closed.

reuse_for_v5.v5_part: Gate W / Part 16 (sandbox, evaluator isolation, reward hacking, accounting, network, private state)
reuse_for_v5.how: Reuse the redteam framework unchanged: three-phase contract, ProbeViolation guard on system_call, integrity_postcheck override, KNOWN_OPEN ratchet and toy sanity check. Its 81 probes already cover reward hacking, metric inflation, accounting integrity, evaluator isolation, hidden-answer extraction, sandbox filesystem/network and cross-tenant signalling. Add social and cross-world probe modules and run the suite with a v5 civilization world factory. examples/redteam_report.py already emits machine-readable evidence.

reuse_for_v5.v5_part: Part 16 real-world boundary (adapter disabled by default, authorization, budgets)
reuse_for_v5.how: Keep crucible.realworld as the real-world adapter. It is off without an operator file and has allow-lists, resource budgets, live approval, a hash-chained log and sealed-holdout budgets. tests/test_realworld_gate.py (14 tests) is the acceptance evidence, including a NetworkGuard proof that a default process makes no network connection. Wire forbid_in_this_process into world-hosting entrypoints.

reuse_for_v5.v5_part: Gate P / Part 10.4 (30/90/180/365-day runs, invariants, snapshot/resume, replay)
reuse_for_v5.how: Reuse run_long + InvariantMonitor + examples/long_run4.py for multi-seed runs: relative liveness with proximate causes, recorded shocks, snapshot/resume, final replay digest and per-day CSV. Recorded 90/180/365-day 4.0 runs serve as baselines. Extend the recorder and invariants to social activity and run at the v5 population profiles.

reuse_for_v5.v5_part: Gate L / Part 10.3 (multi-stage chains with counterfactual removal)
reuse_for_v5.how: Reuse invention_trial/invention_suite. It provides matched forks from one snapshot, order 0-4 placement by causal position, no_response and removal arms, fades_after, per-seed proportion CIs and participant provenance labels (scripted / LLM / trained). Reuse fork_compare and emergence.useful_novelty for single-artifact removal, and open_internet.ablate for mechanism ablations. Extend the census to social, content and research tables to get the required social and technical chains.

Reuse the Mechanism dataclass, the REGISTER-per-module mapping, validate_register's refusal of evidence-free calibration claims, and the uncovered_modules coverage test. Migrate the 4 statuses to the 6 v5 levels, add population/platform/time-period/limitations fields, and add entries for entry, use, rig and all v5 modules.

The KNOWN_OPEN ratchet makes any new probe that reports a finding fail tests/test_redteam.py unless it is listed with severity and fix. MUST_HOLD (tests/test_redteam.py:18) pins 21 probes that must report held.

A custom world factory that lacks a kwarg a probe requests (e.g. open_world, consumers, family) makes the probe report not_applicable (framework.py:428-430), not held. A v5 red-team report must count NA rows, not just findings.

Exactness: forks and fork-vs-parent equality are exact only with params.cost_model == 'deterministic'. Under measured CPU cost two forks diverge, and invention_trial/fork_compare report exact=False. The deterministic model undercounts native-code work (LIMITATIONS.md:30-32).

Intervention with params (set_params) mutates world.spec.params in place and emits an internal 'note' event whose applier is a no-op (core/kernel.py:385). From code reading, an intervened fork cannot be reproduced by replaying spec + log. Not verified by running.

Store-less worlds keep every event alive in World._unflushed even after log trimming (kernel.py:571, flush only at :877-880). run_long creates worlds without a store, so long v5 runs will grow memory roughly linearly with events (365-day 4.0 runs already peaked at 1.36-1.58 GB RSS).
_Recorder.on_event serialises every event with json.dumps just to count log bytes (longrun.py:120), a per-event cost that grows with v5 event volume.

determinism_replay_persistence:
Worlds are event-sourced and hash-chained, so replay is exact. World.replay(spec, events, world_id='replay', verify=True, base_blob=None) re-applies events and checks the chain (core/kernel.py:956). Snapshots are World.snapshot_blob() (pickle protocol 5 plus zlib, holding spec, world_id, seq, hash, state and kernel version), loaded with World.from_blob.

The assurance code uses this in five places:
- integrity_postcheck replays from genesis after every probe, but only when log_base == 0 and seq <= 400,000, and compares digest and last_hash.
- run_long replays at the end: from genesis, from base_blob for forks or resumed runs, or skips when the log is trimmed. It snapshots every N days to <label>.snap with the harness state in <label>.state.pkl, written via tmp + os.replace.
- invention_trial and fork_compare fork from one snapshot blob and can re-run the control arm to check determinism (check_determinism=True). Forks are exact only under cost_model='deterministic', which is reported as 'exact'.
- Counterfactual interventions are recorded system calls, so the intervened fork's log states what changed. The exception is set_params (an internal no-op note).
- Shocks go through the operator-only Disturb tools as recorded commands, so disturbed runs replay and regenerate.

Real-world persistence is separate: an append-only blake2b-16 chained JSONL log with fsync per record, verified on open and never extended when corrupt. Request and byte budgets, wall time and holdout counts are re-derived from the log, so they survive restarts.

Store-level tamper evidence: the chain alone cannot detect a rewritten suffix or a truncated tail (the open finding). storage.base.make_anchor/verify_anchor can detect both, but no harness calls them.

The in-memory log keeps 2M events (spec param log_retain); older events must come from the store (events_range raises ProtocolError without one). census move detection and the fidelity _events() helper read the in-memory log.
